title.narrative: Eradication of child labour in ginger production

description.narrative: This project focuses on elaboration of child labour in Nigerian ginger production. It is an effort of a consortium consisting of Catz International, Verstegen Spices & Sauces and Koninklijke Nederlandse Specerijenvereniging in the Netherlands, and ginger processors/exporters AFEX, GACON and Shield of Women in Nigeria. Local interventions are implemented by the Fair Labor Association in collaboration with Crudan-Nigeria. The selection for Nigeria, Kaduna State (ginger), is mainly based on the fact that child labour at farmer's level is considered a major risk.Objectives:1. The number of children under the age of 15 involved in ginger production is reduced;2. The number of young workers above the age of 15 and under the age of 18 (both children of farmers and migrant workers) involved in hazardous activities in ginger production is reduced;3. Labour conditions of young workers in the age of 15-18 (who are not involved in hazardous activities) is improved (International Labour Organization (ILO) decent work standards will be applied as a reference);4. The ginger producers' household income has increased; and5. At least one supply chain, linking ginger farmer(s) community(ies), Nigerian processor(s)/exporter(s) and Dutch buyers, is very likely to be 'child labour free'.The project B has four main work packages:A. Strengthening due diligence management and sustainable sourcing policies of Nigerian ginger processors/exporters and Dutch buyers;B. Awareness raising and training activities at the farmers' level and other local stakeholders;C. Economic empowerment of ginger farmers' households, including Good Agricultural Practice training, creation of Village Savings and Loan Association and implementation of Village Savings and Loan Associations and implementation of three ginger demo plots to showcase possibilities for ginger-blight free production; andD. Identification and dissemination of lessons learned and development of action plan for continuous efforts to contribute to eradication of child labour after the subsidy period.

comment.narrative: The assessment identified 1214 (71%) children aged 6 to 17. Among them, 611 (50%) including 269 males (44%) and 342 females (56%) are enrolled in formal education in Ankwa and Fai. Meaning that 603 (35%) of this age range including 273 male (45%) ans 330 females (55%) were not enrolled in school at the time of the baseline assessment

This objective is revised considering new challenges in the project. 65% of ginger producers' school age children are enrolled in school, including 50% in Ankwa and 80% in Fai. No distinction will be made between males and females. The only criteria will be the age for schooling.
